4) Procurement: procurement team will confirm SSO/KMS requirements and procurement timeline.

Notes from call (high level):

- We discussed normalization options — Redwood supports transmitting pre-normalized vectors and/or applying L2 normalization at indexing time; primary tradeoff is cost vs. storage.

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>

Hi Alex — quick answers inline to keep the sync efficient:

1) Mixed vector dims: Yes, Redwood can serve multiple indexes with different vector dimensions concurrently. Each index is versioned and pinned to a schema that includes vector dim. The primary consideration: larger-dim indexes consume more memory per vector and may require different instance classes for optimal throughput. Practically, we recommend keeping the reranker (1024) on higher-memory nodes and the 768 search index on standard nodes.

2) Batching/throughput suggestion for 5M vectors / 6 hours (~230k vectors/hour):
- Recommended batching: 512-2048 vectors per request depending on average vector size and network MTU; start with 1024 and validate.
- Parallel workers: aim for 3-6 concurrent writers per GPU worker for optimal GPU upload pipeline; scale up number of workers to meet total throughput.
- Target throughput: for Dedicated pool with A100-equivalent instances (we use normalized perf numbers), expect ~50-150k vectors/minute per cluster depending on instance type and quantization. For your 5M in 6 hours, a small Dedicated cluster (2-4 GPUs) should be enough if using larger batch sizes and parallel upload. We'll give a specific sizing matrix in the migration plan attachment.

3) Normalization cost/quality:
- If you pre-normalize and store L2-normalized vectors, you save server-side CPU cost at index-time. Storage is identical (vector bytes), but if you avoid server-side normalization you reduce ingestion CPU and slightly reduce per-vector ingestion cost.
- Quality: identical if normalization math is identical. Slight differences can occur due to float precision/quantization, but we haven't seen material ranking drift when clients provide normalized vectors.

I'll attach a short doc with recommended batch sizes and a sample cURL and Python SDK snippet for bulk-upsert. Also added a thumb-rule for memory vs dim.

Happy to cover details Thursday; what time works for Samir?
